messages:
sam: Heads-up — billing alert: ~$28k unplanned GPU spend in the last hour. Looks like autoscaler spun up ~40 on-demand A100 instances in us-west1 instead of our reserved pool. Anyone seeing this?

maria: Oof. Can you paste the billing lines or export?

sam: Billing export shows SKU lines for "GPU (A100) OnDemand" and no matching "Committed Use Discount" entries. Also the instances were `gpu-fallback-*` names (on-demand).

sam: Console snippets: https://console.cloud.google.com/billing/charges?cid=redacted (short link)

ari: Did the nodepool label `reserved=redwood-a100` get dropped in the last apply? I saw a terraform merge earlier this morning.

liz: I just ran `kubectl get nodes -L reserved | grep -v redwood-a100` — several prod nodes returned with blank `reserved` label.

liz: Quick check: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="name:gpu-fallback*" --format="table(name,machineType,labels)"` shows machineType `n1-standard-32-a100` (on-demand) instead of our `a2-highgpu-*` reserved family.

sam: I pulled the terraform plan from the PR merged at 18:32. Diff shows the node_pool block where `node_labels = { reserved = "redwood-a100" }` was accidentally replaced with `labels = {}`. Looks like a variable rename bug.

ari: That explains it — autoscaler fallback policy will try to satisfy scale requests in any compatible instance family if the named reserved pool isn't present. It launched on-demand machines in the same zone.

maria: Finance note: our committed reservations only apply when instances are created in the dedicated reserved node pool and carry the tag `billing_commitment=west-a100-60`. Without the label/tag the charges are full on-demand.

ari: Immediate action plan: 1) Pause autoscaler on the affected cluster 2) Revert terraform change and reapply node labels 3) Recreate nodes to pick up reserved pool 4) Open emergency billing case for retroactive credits.

liz: I've paused the autoscaler and started cordoning/draining the extra nodes. `kubectl cordon gpu-fallback-* && kubectl drain gpu-fallback-* --ignore-daemonsets` in progress.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler paused on cluster-prod-us-west1 by @liz :white_check_mark:

sam: Maria — can you open the emergency support ticket with cloud provider and include the exact window and billing CSV? P0 please.

maria: Ticket created: #INC-1428. Included terraform plan, node names, and timestamps. Asking for retroactive CUD credits and a temporary invoice hold.

ari: I'll push a TF revert and add a CI validation to fail if node labels for `reserved` are empty (GH Actions + tfsec style check). Also adding an autoscaler test that simulates missing pool to ensure it fails safe.

sam: Please also attach autoscaler logs and the scaling events: `/var/log/autoscaler/scale-events.log` — looks like a burst of scale-ups at 18:28.

liz: Terminations completed, remaining extraneous nodes are down and workloads moved. Cluster utilization back to expected.

maria: Finance will follow up after cloud provider responds. Preliminary estimate: $28k gross, we expect some credits — tagging internal cost bucket for now.

sam: I'll start a postmortem doc (link coming). We need root cause, timeline, and prevention (CI check + tf review checklist).

ari: Long-term: consider autoscaler policy change to never fallback to non-reserved families for prod clusters, and require an explicit opt-in.

liz: Agreed. Also adding an alert to billing streamer when on-demand GPU SKU spikes over a threshold.

maria: Noted. I'll coordinate finance + legal for contractual follow-up once credits confirmed.

sam: Thanks all — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
